title: Optimize Console: Recommendation cardflow with risk scoring and revert audit trail
creator: Maya Chen
description: Scope: Build a cohesive card-driven flow in the Optimize Console that surfaces batching/caching recommendations with an inline risk score and a time-ordered revert audit trail. Goals: 1) Make it obvious why a suggestion reduces cost and the expected token savings; 2) Surface confidence and risk signals (quality regressions, latency trade-offs) so PMs/engineers can safely accept recommendations; 3) Provide a single-click safe-apply that records an immutable audit entry and a reversible revert action with provenance metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards display: summary, estimated monthly token savings, confidence score, and dominant customer-visible risk (latency/regression)
Diff preview pane shows before/after config with tokenized cost delta and per-route impact estimates
Safe-apply action creates an immutable audit entry with user, timestamp, commit id, and can be reverted within 30 days via a recorded revert event
Audit trail UI supports filtering by user, date range, recommendation type, and shows linked PR/Runbook when available
Telemetry hooks emit events for card impressions, preview opens, safe-apply attempts, reverts, and fallout (quality alert)
notes: Initial spike found three risk heuristics: model-perf delta, p50 latency uplift, and cache warmup sensitivity.
Backend work needed: provenance blob in config apply API (schema v2) and eventing for audit entries.
Design asked for compact and expanded card states to reduce cognitive load on lists > 6 items.
